title: Socio-economic landscape of digital transformation & public NLP systems: A critical review

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative evaluation using a political-economic lens to analyze how NLP systems impact labor dynamics, platformization, and decision-making algorithms (such as creditworthiness scoring), shifting costs and precariousness onto vulnerable members of society.

Normative and function-creep analysis of NLP and machine learning systems used in predictive policing and the judicial system (e.g., COMPAS), evaluating how these tools replicate historical patterns of discrimination and over-policing against racial minorities.

Qualitative analysis of the labor conditions surrounding NLP data production (e.g., crowdwork), noting how the resulting job insecurity and precariousness disproportionately affect women due to dual exploitation in domestic and professional spheres.
